jobs.description:
About Heraeus

Making displays foldable? Helping hearts beat with medical innovations? Or breathing new life into precious metals? As a family-owned global technology group we help our customers to always being one step ahead.

About Heraeus Medevio

Together we improve lives. At Heraeus Medevio, we bring lifesaving and life-changing medical devices to market through partnerships with medical device manufacturing companies. Backed by Heraeus Group, we are committed to the growth of our teams and organization by providing an open space for open minds.

To reach our vision of improving 100 million lives every year, we foster a culture of curiosity that thrives on challenge, continuous learning, growth, and the opportunity to try new things. With sites in the United States, European Union, and Asia, and over 2,200 employees worldwide, together, we will meet tomorrow's challenges today.

The following challenges await you:

- You work in many areas of interventional devices, including access devices, advanced diagnostic and therapeutic catheters and complex delivery systems, applying state-of-the-art technology.
- In your role, you are the technical lead in development projects for catheters and other interventional devices with a customer-specific design from concept freeze throughout product design and manufacturing transfer to the manufacturing sites.
- You work in cross-functional teams with program managers, design and process development engineers, prototyping technicians, documentation specialists and RA/QA representatives within the global footprint of our company, as well as with our business partners and customers.
- You support the project managers to structure development projects, forming high potential teams.
- You take over responsibility for the technical design and for meeting specification and performance requirements with a strong focus on design-to-manufacture (DfM).
- You develop and build prototypes - draft and hands-on - designed for safe and effective use to improve the well-being of patients worldwide.
- You develop test methods for bench testing, design verification and simulated use validation
- You ensure complete engineering documentation according to regulations, standards and industry best practices under design control, using office documents and our paperless PLM system.
- You keep stakeholders, customers, and others informed of the project status and upcoming issues.
- You guide and mentor less experienced team members

Your profile:

- Bachelor’s degree in biomedical engineering, mechanical engineering, plastics engineering, or a related field, preferably master’s,
- A minimum of 5 years of relevant professional experience in the medical device development environment,
- Proven experience in developing catheters or other interventional devices (e.g., through projects, patents, publications) and in-depth knowledge of catheter design and materials as well as related manufacturing technologies (e.g., extrusion, thermoforming, laser processing) with a focus on design-to-manufacture,
- Knowledge of design control and regulatory requirements according to ISO 13485 / FDA 21 CFR Part 820 and other applicable catheter standards,
- Experience with design and process risk management (FMEA), design verification and simulated use testing,
- Ability to make data-driven decisions utilizing statistical tools such as DOE, tolerance stack-up analysis, or Minitab,
- Experienced worker in interdisciplinary and intercultural teams (e.g., quality, regulatory affairs, production) including mentoring of team members,
- Good command of English, both written and spoken,
- Structured, solution-oriented working style with a high level of personal responsibility,
- Able to travel occasionally to customers, study locations or other company sites throughout the world.

Curious? Apply now!

We are interested in finding the best candidates, and they may come from a nontraditional background. So please don’t hesitate to apply, even if you aren’t an exact fit. We look forward to getting you started on your employment journey with Heraeus Medevio!

Any further questions?

Our Recruiting Team, Heraeus Medevio, is happy to assist you by email: recruiting.medevio@heraeus.com. Or visit us at jobs.heraeus.com (https://javascript:void(0);) .

jobs.occupation: (Senior) Manager Direct Tax Compliance & Processes (m/f/d) (Betriebswirt/in (Hochschule) - Steuern und Prüfungswesen)
jobs.description:
Overview  

 
At QIAGEN, we are driven by a simple but powerful vision: making improvements in life possible.  

We’re dedicated to revolutionizing science and healthcare for the better. From our entrepreneurial roots to our current global presence, we've grown into a force for positive change. With thousands of employees across six continents, collaboration is our greatest strength. We’re always striving to identify talented individuals to join our exceptional teams. 
 
We have played a pivotal role in shaping modern science and healthcare, and we're just getting started. If you're someone who thrives on new challenges, values diversity and wants to make a tangible difference in people's lives, then QIAGEN is the place for you. 

 

At QIAGEN, every day is an opportunity to make a real-life impact. 

 

Join us, grow with us, and together, let's shape the future of biological discovery. 

‎

About the opportunity

As (Senior) Manager Direct Tax Compliance & Processes, you will act as a trusted business partner to management, driving efficiency and effectiveness across tax compliance, accounting, and reporting activities. You will play a key role in enhancing QIAGEN's tax compliance and governance framework, supporting our tax compliance insourcing strategy, and advancing tax quality and change management initiatives. This position offers the opportunity to collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders while contributing to tax reporting, compliance, process optimization, and strategic tax projects across the DACH region.

Your tasks
* Further develop and enhance the Tax Compliance Management System while proactively supporting tax governance, tax quality, and change management initiatives.
* Support annual tax reporting at both legal entity and group level, including the calculation of tax positions and preparation of tax-related disclosures under US GAAP and local GAAP requirements.
* Manage direct tax return and compliance processes in collaboration with external advisors across the DACH region.
* Oversee additional tax compliance obligations within the DACH region and maintain the tax compliance calendar.
* Manage inbound and outbound withholding tax matters, including reporting and filing requirements, while identifying and implementing process improvements.
* Serve as a key business partner for Accounting, Treasury, Legal, Operations, and other internal stakeholders on tax-related matters.
* Support tax audits, tax planning activities, and corporate tax restructuring projects.

Your profile
* University degree in Business Administration, Economics (with a focus on Tax and/or Accounting), Tax Administration (Finanzwirt) or a comparable qualification.
* At least 5 years of relevant professional experience gained within an international advisory firm (e.g., Big 4) and/or the tax function of a multinational organization.
* Strong understanding of direct tax compliance, tax accounting, and tax reporting requirements.
* Proven ability to work independently with a high level of accuracy, diligence, and quality awareness.
* Experience with Microsoft Office applications as well as tax and ERP systems such as DATEV and SAP.
* Professional proficiency in English and German with strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Collaborative team player with strong stakeholder management and influencing skills.

What we offer  

 

* Bonus/Commission  

* Local benefits   

* Referral Program  

* Volunteer Day  

* Internal Academy (QIALearn)   

* Employee Assistance Program   

* Hybrid work (conditional to your role) 

 

Our people are the heartbeat of everything we do. Passion drives us as we push boundaries to innovate and evolve. We inspire with our leadership and make an impact with our actions. We cultivate a collaborative, supportive environment where each individual and team can flourish. We champion accountability and encourage entrepreneurial thinking.   

 

QIAGEN is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, or disability.

jobs.occupation: Robotics Manufacturing Engineer, Line Design, Geartrain (Automobil-Fachwirt/in)
jobs.description:
What to Expect

In this role you’ll support the design, construction, launch, and transfer of geartrain manufacturing lines and equipment used in Optimus Actuators. This role will prioritize successful design and launch of production line while maintaining maximum efficiency, production volume, and safety while validating performance and fully documenting all aspects of the project for handover to sustaining operations.  The ideal candidate will bring deep technical expertise in high-volume geartrain manufacturing lines and the successful introduction of new technologies to mass production line. They must demonstrate experience translating manufacturing requirements into efficient, detailed production line designs that are robust and practical to implement . In this position, you will take ownership of production line creation of specialized equipment from concept through line launch completion—defining performance requirements, running process flow simulations as needed to validate solutions grounded in first principles, and leading commissioning through final validation.

What You’ll Do

- Use CAD software and simulation tools (e.g., AutoCAD, FactoryCAD, or similar) to create 2D/3D models, floor plans, and detailed drawings that support both main production line and also supporting areas within Geartrain Manufacturing Scope
- Work with factory simulation/modeling teams to develop flow manufacturing constraints for new equipment development such as aisle sizing, incoming raw materials to the cell and work in progress areas between cells
- Install, commission, integrate and troubleshoot new equipment and tooling and support setup for manufacturing, including machines, peripheral equipment, tools, and automation systems
- Oversee the handover of commissioned lines to production teams, including operator training, documentation of procedures and manufacturing BOM, and resolution of issues during line launch
- Contribute to R&D efforts in equipment design and process development by integrating layout considerations, material flow, and facility requirements early in the innovation cycle to enable scalable and efficient manufacturing solutions
- Design and develop detailed cell and production line layouts for each gearbox, including placement of machinery and their integration to the mainline, workstations, material flow paths, utilities, and storage areas to optimize production processes and efficiency
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Factory, Infrastructure, Material Flow, Design, Manufacturing Eng., EHS personnel, and project&program leads) to integrate layouts into main factory design
- Ensure compliance with Tesla safety regulations, ergonomic standards, and lean manufacturing principles while evaluating new equipment and processes from R&D initiatives
- Evaluate data on production performance, material handling, and space utilization to recommend layout improvements that align with ongoing R&D advancements in equipment and manufacturing processes
- Design custom fixtures, tooling, and other structures that would be used in manufacturing cells as needed, providing detailed build to print models/drawings for fabrication

What You’ll Bring

- Degree in Industrial Engineering or a related field (advanced degree or relevant certifications are a plus), or equivalent industry experience and evidence of exceptional ability
- Several years of experience in manufacturing or industrial engineering, with hands-on involvement in factory/plant layout projects
- Proficiency in layout design software, process simulation tools, and data analysis
- Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, material flow, ergonomics, and facility safety standards
- Experience designing layouts, mechanical equipment, fixturing, and tooling
- Knowledge in high speed gantry design including the pick and place into conveyor systems
- Knowledge in material flow analysis and basic knowledge about different industrial robots in high speed material transfer and pick and place applications
- Experience with SolidWorks CAD and PDM software. Familiarity with other CAD software (i.e CATIA, Siemens NX) also applies
- Experience with automation equipment, CNC equipment, heat treatment, assembly and end of line testing equipment
- Strong understanding of drafting standards and the application of GD&T (e.g., ASME Y14.5)
- Ability to communicate at a professional level in English language, both verbally and written
- Ability to travel internationally on a regular basis

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, gender identity or any other factor protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.

What to Expect

The Tesla Robotics Team designs and builds humanoid bi-pedal robots (Optimus) to perform tasks that are boring, repetitive, and dangerous for humans. As a CAE Engineer, you will guide the design of sensors and structural components using high-fidelity FE models grounded in sound engineering principles Working closely with mechanical, electrical, controls, software, and manufacturing teams, you’ll analyze and optimize designs, challenge traditional CAE methods, and pioneer more efficient, accurate approaches. This role places you at the forefront of critical design and engineering decisions, shaping a robust and reliable humanoid robot that has never been executed before.

What You’ll Do

- Develop and analyze comprehensive Finite Element (FE) models for Optimus, from individual components to the full system
- Conduct static, dynamic, structural and MBD simulations to evaluate and validate the performance against key requirements for strength, stiffness, durability and sensing
- Build and refine simulation workflows to assess performance across diverse operating scenarios, automate processes, documentation, and tools to improve efficiency, accuracy, and repeatability
- Provide design guidance to world-class engineering teams, enabling data-driven product decisions
- Collaborate with Test Engineering to design and validate experiments, correlate test data with simulations, and enhance predictive modeling capabilities
- Establish and maintain modeling standards, methods, and best practices for current and future programs
- Material characterization and advanced modeling of structural and sensing components
- Plan and execute large-scale DOEs, creating ML driven surrogate models to extract insights to drive key design decisions

What You’ll Bring

- Degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience
- Strong foundation in Engineering Mechanics, Computational Mechanics, Material Science, and Finite Element Theory and applications
- Demonstrated ability to guide structural, sensing, thermal, and mechanism designs through CAE, from concept to mass production, across robotics, automotive, and consumer electronics
- Expertise in building high-fidelity FE models at component, sub-system, and full-system levels
- Proficiency in linear and non-linear static, dynamic and modal simulations and experience developing multi-physics simulation workflows (e.g., thermal-mechanical, mechanical-electrical)
- Advanced knowledge in material characterization and modeling, including nonlinear elasticity, viscoelasticity, creep, and strain-rate dependent plasticity in Metals, Plastics, Polymers and Adhesives
- Proficiency in CAE Tools such as BETA CAE, LS-DYNA, Abaqus, ADAMS, COMSOL, OPTISTRUCT, Design Life, FE Safe
- Strong programming and data analysis skills in MATLAB, Python, or equivalent
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams
- Ability to communicate at a professional level in English language, both verbally and written
- Ability to travel internationally on a regular basis

jobs.occupation: Robotics Geartrain Manufacturing Engineer, Optimus Actuators (Automobil-Fachwirt/in)
jobs.description:
What to Expect

Optimus actuator team is seeking a skilled and highly motivated, engineer with gearbox manufacturing, design, assembly, machining and metrology experience to join the team. We work with the cross-functional teams (Design, Quality, Production, Sustaining, and Supply Chain) throughout the entire lifecycle of a product (from initial design through prototype development and into full production) to develop volume manufacturable designs and processes that will produce gearboxes. The role of the Gearbox Manufacturing Engineer is to support gearbox manufacturing process development to produce world-class gearbox prototypes and drive scalable production methods to high volume production. The ideal candidate takes pride in their work, has excellent engineering and physics fundamentals, is excited about manufacturing process development, does not shy away from a challenge, highly organized, has good great attention to detail, and is able to work in fast paced development environment with analytical and practical engineering focus.

What You’ll Do

- Drive the in-house manufacturing technology and process development of complex gear assemblies
- Develop scalable manufacturing technologies that can scale from concept to high-volume production for gearboxes
- Drive demonstration of developed gearbox manufacturing processes in a low volume, high-mix environment
- Establish equipment requirements for high volume gearbox manufacturing and develop high-volume manufacturing methods Drive machine tool equipment and tooling design developments with external suppliers and with internal entities for scalable high-volume (automotive level) production
- Develop specifications and manage RFQ process for new manufacturing equipment
- Design and build tooling that will be used gearbox assembly processes
- Work closely with design engineering team to provide crucial input on DFM and DFA
- Track and document process development activities on geartrain assembly, machining and heat treatment processes and report results when necessary
- Develop equipment manufacturing, heat treatment, inspection, and test validation plans
- Coordinate factory equipment installation, commissioning, and production hand off

What You’ll Bring

- Degree in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent, or equivalent experience
- Mindset to apply first principles for problem solving
- 3D CAD experience/knowledge, preferably Catia/3DX, SolidWorks. Familiarity with computer aided manufacturing software (i.e. Mastercam, Esprit) and gear design & manufacturing software (i.e. KissSoft, Dontyne Gear Production Suite) is plus 
- Knowledge and understanding of engineering drawings, documents and GD&T. Ability to follow mechanical drawings of assemblies and components that include bearings, gearboxes, actuators, etc.
- Proficiency in mechanical assemblies of gearboxes (i.e press fits, fastener selection, etc.) and knowledge and understanding of gear metrology tools and methods
- Familiar with torque tools, fixture design, CNC and automation equipment, control systems and communication protocol
- Strong background in mechanical design for manufacturing and basic principles of material science & engineering with experience in transitioning products from prototype to high-volume production
- Knowledge of material heat treatment basics and familiarity with failure analysis of heat treated components. Hands on experience of operating heat treatment equipment (i.e. induction hardening station)
- Several years of experience in heat treatment, metallurgical processes and heat treatment inspection methods Extensive knowledge of heat treatment processes and equipment
- Several years of experience building production lines for geared products. Including, equipment design, tooling design, design of process flows that includes heat treatment, procurement and line commissioning
- Ability to communicate at a professional level in English language, both verbally and written
- Ability to travel internationally on a regular basis

jobs.description:
What to Expect

The Optimus geartrain manufacturing team is seeking a skilled and highly motivated, mechanical equipment design engineer with high precision equipment build experience within gearbox, electric motor or other industries focusing on rotating machinery design and manufacturing. We work with the cross-functional teams (Design, Quality, Production, Sustaining, Automation, and Supply Chain) throughout the entire lifecycle of a product (from initial design through prototype development and into full production) to develop volume manufacturable designs and processes that will produce gearboxes. The role of the equipment design engineer is to support establishing a world-class production line for gearboxes and drive scalable design and production methods used to make “the machines that make the machines”.   The ideal candidate takes pride in their work, has excellent engineering and physics fundamentals with hands on experience, is excited about manufacturing equipment and process development, does not shy away from a challenge, highly organized, has great attention to detail, and is able to work in fast paced development environment with analytical and practical engineering focus.   

What You’ll Do

- Own design of equipment builds through their entire lifecycle, from initial concept generation through assembly and production bring-up
- Prepare overall machine design concepts for custom designed, special purpose manufacturing equipment and systems
- Detailed machine design including drawings of custom automated tooling, fixtures, mechanisms, robotic end of arm tooling etc.
- Detailed engineering analysis of custom mechanical components including hand calculations and finite element analysis
- Selection and integration of commercial components, sensors, motors, pneumatic, hydraulic actuators, etc. 
- Conduct design reviews for internal team feedback and for cross-functional presentations. Be a liaison between actuator, gearbox, design and manufacturing engineering departments 
- Lead all technical conversations with sub-system or supporting equipment suppliers
- Create detailed drawings and coordinate with internal and external machine shops to fabricate custom machined parts, weldments, extrusions and sheet metal components
- Work with technician teams to assemble and commission new equipment 
- Validate equipment performance and reliability. Create comprehensive equipment handover packages and system documentation 

What You’ll Bring

- Extensive experience as a Mechanical Engineer 
- Experience with SolidWorks CAD and PDM software. Familiarity with other CAD software (i.e. CATIA, Siemens NX) also applies
- Experience with automation equipment design and custom machine building. Familiarity with instrumentation used during high precision equipment build. (i.e. laser alignment devices) 
- Experience with various manufacturing processes (i.e., assembly, fastening, dispensing, laser welding)
- Strong understanding of drafting standards and the application of GD&T (e.g., ASME Y14.5) 
- Familiarity with design and troubleshooting of rotating machinery. i.e. systems with bearings
- Familiarity with specifying systems based on torque & power curves of electric motors or systems integrated with gearboxes
- Experience using finite element software for structural analysis

jobs.occupation: Lead Human Pharma Public & Government Afffairs (Obesity and Metabolic Health) (Leiter/in - Public Affairs (Lobbying))
jobs.employer_name: Boehringer Ingelheim Pharma GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description:
Boehringer Ingelheim is a biopharmaceutical company active in both human and animal health. As one of the industry's top investors in research and development, the company focuses on developing innovative therapies that can improve and extend lives in areas of high unmet medical need. Independent since its foundation in 1885, Boehringer takes a long-term perspective, embedding sustainability along the entire value chain. Our approximately 54,500 employees serve over 130 markets to build a healthier and more sustainable tomorrow. Learn more at www.boehringer-ingelheim.com
The Position
As Lead Human Pharma Public & Government Affairs Obesity and Metabolic Health you will join a dynamic team dedicated to engaging with policymakers around the world to enable the access and uptake of life-changing pharmaceutical innovation. As part of the Public & Government Affairs function in the Corporate Affairs division, you will deliver integrated campaigns to drive meaningful policy change in particular areas of healthcare. At this time, we especially welcome applications from candidates with experience in policy shaping focused on Obesity and Metabolic Health, the therapeutic focus can shift in role based on business need.
This position is based at our Global Headquarters in Ingelheim, Germany.
Tasks & responsibilities

- As the Public & Government Affairs Lead for Obesity and Metabolic Health, in alignment with colleagues in the Corporate Affairs division, you will ensure we develop and implement integrated campaigns. In support of our established portfolio and future launches, you will establish alliances for awareness raising and targeted policy prioritization.
- One of your key tasks will be policy and stakeholder mapping to ensure the company has an informed position for key therapeutic areas within the Human Pharma business. You will lead on the creation of clear policy positions and support wider evidence generation to enable global and country teams to engage with policymakers.
- You will enable Public & Government Affairs capabilities and execution with a particular focus on the EU5, US, China and Japan.
- Moreover, you will support the Head of HP Public & Government Affairs to coach country teams in the development of clear strategic and tactical plans with measurable policy outcomes.
- You will be the main contact person for assigned Therapeutic Areas and other partners in the Human Pharma business. You will provide clear strategic counsel and be recognized as an expert in international health policy and country-level policy change.

Ultrasonic Acoustic Engineer (m/f/d)

Sound Propagation, Resonance & Biofouling Prevention

HASYTEC (Ultrasonic Tech GmbH, part of the ERMA TECH Group) develops and markets highly innovative ultrasonic technology that prevents biofouling on fluid-carrying surfaces. Our systems protect more than 300 ships, offshore platforms, and maritime installations worldwide against barnacles, algae, and mussels—efficiently, sustainably, and with minimal maintenance.

To strengthen our development team, we are looking for an Ultrasonic Acoustics Engineer who is passionate about understanding sound propagation, resonance behaviour and ultrasonic systems in complex maritime structures.

You will help develop the next generation of ultrasonic anti-fouling technology.

Our long-term goal is to protect not only piping systems and sea water equipment, but also large ship hull structures through controlled ultrasonic resonance fields.

Your responsibilities include:

- Analyze ultrasonic wave propagation in maritime structures and materials
- Investigate resonance behaviour in piping systems, sea chests, strainers, box coolers, propeller systems and hull structures
- Develop and optimize ultrasonic transducer configurations and installation concepts
- Plan, execute and evaluate laboratory experiments and onboard vessel trials
- Measure vibration behaviour and acoustic transmission using modern test equipment
- Analyze experimental data and derive practical design improvements
- Collaborate with hardware, software and mechanical engineering teams
- Coordinate technical activities with universities and research institutes

Technical Qualifications

- Degree in Physics, Acoustics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics or a related field
- Experience in one or more of the following: - Ultrasonics
- Acoustics
- Vibration analysis
- Resonance behaviour
- Signal processing
- Experimental testing
- Experience with laboratory measurement equipment such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers or vibration measurement systems
- Experience in data analysis using Python, MATLAB or similar tools
- Experience in maritime systems, fluid-carrying structures or piezoelectric technology is beneficial but not required
- Analytical and systematic working style
- Curiosity for understanding physical phenomena
- Hands-on mentality and enthusiasm for experimental work
- Ability to bridge theory and practical application
- Team-oriented mindset and initiative
- Our working language is English

What Makes This Role Unique

This is not a standard engineering position.

You will work on challenging acoustic problems involving sound propagation, structural resonance and ultrasonic excitation in real maritime applications.

The role combines physics, experimentation, onboard testing and collaboration with leading research institutions to develop sustainable technologies for the maritime industry.

What we Offer

Ref.-Nr.  601-2026
Third-party funding

The Faculty of Medicine is an integral part of the Otto-von-Guericke-University Magdeburg and cooperates with the Magdeburg University Hospital A.ö.R. in research, teaching and patient care.

Your Responsibilities:

We are seeking two highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Fellows to join our team investigating the molecular and cellular organization of the nervous system using cutting-edge spatial transcriptomics approaches. The successful candidates will work at the interface of neuroscience, genomics, and computational biology to map gene expression patterns across brain tissue with spatial resolution, contributing to our understanding of neural circuit organization, development, and disease.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a collaborative, well-resourced research environment with access to state-of-the-art spatial profiling platforms (e.g., MERFISH, 10x Visium), advanced microscopy, and high-performance computing infrastructure.

Two positions are available with complementary focus:

- Position 1 — Experimental/Wet-lab focus: Designing and executing spatial transcriptomics experiments on neural tissue, including tissue preparation, probe design, imaging, and data generation
- Position 2 — Computational/Analytical focus: Developing and applying computational pipelines for spatial transcriptomic data analysis, including cell-type mapping, spatial statistics, and integration with single-cell/single-nucleus datasets

(Candidates with strong interest and skills spanning both areas are also encouraged to apply and may be considered for either position.)

Key Responsibilities:

- Design, plan, and conduct spatial transcriptomics experiments on neural tissue samples
- Analyze and interpret complex spatial and single-cell genomic datasets
- Collaborate with neuroscientists, computational biologists, and clinicians within and outside the group
- Present findings at lab meetings, seminars, and international conferences
- Prepare manuscripts for peer-reviewed publication
- Contribute to grant writing and mentoring of graduate/undergraduate students
- Maintain rigorous documentation and adhere to good research and data management practices

Your Profile:

Essential Qualifications:

- A PhD (completed or close to completion) in Neuroscience, Molecular/Cell Biology, Genomics, Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, or a related field
- Demonstrated research productivity (peer-reviewed publications and/or preprints)
- Strong written and verbal communication skills in English

For the experimental-focus position, in addition:

- Hands-on experience with molecular biology techniques (e.g., histology, immunohistochemistry, in situ hybridization, RNA-seq library prep)
- Experience with spatial transcriptomics platforms (e.g., Visium, MERFISH, Xenium, seqFISH) is highly desirable
- Experience with rodent or human brain tissue handling is a plus

For the computational-focus position, in addition:

- Strong programming skills (Python and/or R)
- Experience analyzing single-cell/single-nucleus RNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics data
- Familiarity with relevant packages/tools (e.g., Scanpy, Seurat, Squidpy, STUtility) and statistical/machine learning methods
- Experience with high-performance/cluster computing is a plus

We offer:

- Access to cutting-edge spatial transcriptomics and imaging technology
- A collaborative, interdisciplinary, and supportive research environment
- Funding and support to attend international conferences
- Opportunities for career development, mentoring, and grant-writing training

Thinking of doing your PhD in the Life Sciences? The International PhD Programme (IPP) Mainz is offering talented scientists the chance to work on cutting edge research projects. As an IPP PhD student, you will join a community of exceptional scientists working on diverse topics ranging from how organisms age or how our DNA is repaired, to how epigenetics regulates cellular identity or neural memory. The research group of Anton Khmelinskii in collaboration with Jan Padeken offers the following PhD project:
The progressive deterioration of protein homeostasis (proteostasis) is a primary hallmark of aging. As organisms age, the functionality of the proteostasis network, comprised of molecular chaperones, the ubiquitin-proteasome system and autophagy, declines, leading to the accumulation of misfolded and aggregated proteins that compromise cellular viability. Proteostatic decline is not merely a consequence of aging but an early, causal event whereby loss of proteostasis precedes and predicts organismal decline, and its onset is sufficient to accelerate aging. Conversely, genetic or pharmacological enhancement of proteostasis network capacity can extend lifespan and suppresses age-related disease associated with protein misfolding across multiple model systems. These observations raise fundamental questions: what endogenous small molecules sustain proteostasis during aging, can their supplementation prevent neurodegenerative (and other protein folding diseases) and slow the aging process?

PhD project: Therapeutic applications of small molecule modulators of proteostasis

Organisms across all domains of life employ the accumulation of small organic osmolytes, which include molecules such as betaine and taurine, to mitigate proteotoxic stress. Recent work has also demonstrated anti-aging properties of this molecules, through yet unclear mechanisms. This project aims at dissecting the mode of action of different osmolytes using human cellular model systems and C. elegans as a model of organismal aging. We would like to address the following questions:

1. How do osmolytes affect cellular and organismal physiology?
2. Which types of stresses can be mitigated with exogenous osmolytes?
3. What types of protein misfolding pathologies (e.g., neurodegenerative diseases including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), Alzheimers's, Parkinson's, Huntington's) can be ameliorated with exogenous osmolytes?

The project is part of an ongoing collaboration between the Khmelinskii and Padeken groups, which gives you the opportunity to become an expert in a wide range of methods and experimental approaches. This includes transcriptomics, proteomics, cell and molecular biology, fluorescence microscopy and advanced high-throughput mutagenesis screening.

If you are interested in this project, please select Khmelinskii/Padeken as your group preference in the IPP application platform. The foundation Max-Planck-Institut für Kohlenforschung in Mülheim an der Ruhr is a renowned research institution that is over 100 years old and has already received two Nobel Prizes in its history. The institute is engaged in basic research in the field of catalysis with the aim of maximizing the efficient use of natural resources.

As a part of the Cluster of Excellence RESOLV (Ruhr Explores Solvation), the Early Career research group “Catalysis” of Dr. Hanna Hinrika Cramer develops organometallic catalysts with earth-abundant first-row transition metals. The team combines experiments, quantum chemistry, and spectroscopy to study reaction mechanisms and to discover how solvation and catalyst design affect the rate and selectivity. Current projects focus on developing well-defined chromium precatalysts for applications in olefin upgrading and the activation of strong bonds.
